title: Data Transforms & Calculated Insights

toc.text: Time math you must know cold
Exercise 1: Translate a requirement to SQL

html:
Harmonization often needs more than field mapping — it needs transforms (batch and streaming) and calculated insights (SQL-defined KPIs). This phase covers the transform tooling, formula fields, and the SQL skills that drive calculated insights, segments, and activation attributes.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Choose batch vs streaming transforms for a requirement.
  • Build a calculated insight as a SQL aggregation over DMOs.
  • Design dimensions and measures, use DATEDIFF/DATEADD/SUM/COUNT in insight SQL.
  • Explain how a calculated insight becomes a profile attribute for segments and activations.
  • Mirror the pattern in CalculatedInsightService and Calculated_Insight__c/KPI_Metric__c.

1. Transforms: batch vs streaming

Transforms change data between ingestion and the DMO (or between DMOs). Two engines:

Batch transformsStreaming transforms
WhenOn the refresh schedule (bulk)On event arrival (near-real-time)
UseHistory reconciliation, large joins, aggregationReal-time metrics, event enrichment
Exam anchor"Which tool refreshes a huge joined DMO nightly?" → batch"Which tool updates a counter as events stream in?" → streaming

A formula field on a DMO is the lightweight sibling: a computed value (e.g. price * qty, IF(opt_out) THEN 'no'). Transforms are heavier: joins, unions, multi-step pipelines.

2. Calculated insights

A calculated insight is an object whose rows are the output of a SQL query over DMOs. It is persisted like data, which means segments can filter on it and activations can publish it.

The mental model: you are creating a metric table.

sql
-- Classic lifetime-value insight
SELECT
    IndividualId,
    SUM(o.totalamount)   AS `Total_Spend`,
    AVG(o.totalamount)   AS `Avg_Order_Value`,
    COUNT(o.id)          AS `Order_Count`,
    DATEDIFF(DAY, MAX(o.createddate), CURRENT_DATE) AS `Days_Since_Last_Order`
FROM Order__dlm AS o
GROUP BY o.IndividualId

Dimensions and measures

  • Measures — the numeric aggregations (SUM, AVG, COUNT, MIN, MAX).
  • Dimensions — the attributes you group by and later filter on (IndividualId, brand, country).
  • Design rule: granularity must match the question. A churn score per customer needs GROUP BY IndividualId; revenue per brand needs GROUP BY brand.

Time math you must know cold

  • DATEDIFF(UNIT, start, end) — days/months between dates.
  • DATEADD(UNIT, n, date) — shift a date (e.g. DATEADD(YEAR, 1, o.createddate)).
  • CURRENT_DATE / CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.
  • Rolling windows via WHERE o.createddate >= DATEADD(DAY, -90, CURRENT_DATE).

Output → reuse

The insight's output columns become attributes on the unified profile ('Total_Spend', 'Churn_Score'). That is why a segment can say Churn_Score >= 0.7, and why an activation can ship Total_Spend to Marketing Cloud. Building the insight before the segment/activation is a required sequencing skill.

3. Writing insight SQL that behaves

Exam and real-world SQL traps:

TrapFix
GROUP BY missing columnsEvery non-aggregate SELECT column must appear in GROUP BY.
NULLs in a SUMSUM(x) ignores NULLs; report them with COUNT(x) vs COUNT(IndividualId).
Date bucketingGroup by DATE_TRUNC(...)/MONTH(createddate) not the raw timestamp.
Joining without keysJOIN ContactPointEmail__dlm c ON c.IndividualId = i.Id — always join on relationship keys.
Ignoring unified vs sourceInsights that should be per-person must GROUP BY IndividualId, and source-level rows alone under-count a person with two records.
Test against sampleAlways LIMIT while iterating a large insight.

The exam frequently shows an SQL snippet and asks what it computes — train yourself to rewrite the query in words ("total order value per individual, last 90 days") before reading the answers.

4. The Lab: CalculatedInsightService

The lab materializes KPI rows instead of running SQL. CalculatedInsightService computes per-account Total_Spend/Order_Count from Account+Opportunity/Order__c-style records and upserts a KPI_Metric__c row — the CRM-side twin of a calculated insight:

apex
public static Map<Id, Decimal> totalSpendByAccount(Set<Id> accountIds) {
    // One selective query, aggregated in memory -> mirrors SELECT SUM(amount) GROUP BY account
    Map<Id, Decimal> sums = new Map<Id, Decimal>();
    for (AggregateResult ar : [SELECT AccountId acct, SUM(Amount) amt
                               FROM Opportunity
                               WHERE AccountId IN :accountIds
                               GROUP BY AccountId]) {
        sums.put((Id) ar.get('acct'), (Decimal) ar.get('amt'));
    }
    return sums;
}

Note the boundary guard (if (accountIds == null || accountIds.isEmpty()) return new Map<>();) and the single-query discipline — the same "one selective statement, then map" habit that makes integration services fast.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Translate a requirement to SQL

"Show me the average order value per customer, restricted to the last 90 days, only for customers with at least 2 orders." Write the calculated-insight SQL (2-step: inner aggregate + outer filter, or HAVING). Use Order__dlm.

Exercise 2: Design measures/dimensions

For Total_Spend, Churn_Score, Avg_Session_Length, Orders_Per_Brand, list the measures and dimensions used by each. State the granularity (per individual? per brand?).

Exercise 3: Extend the service

Add KPI_Metric__c (or Calculated_Insight__c) upsert into CalculatedInsightService following the reference single-DML rule, and write a test that (a) feeds 3 accounts with opportunities, (b) asserts the KPI row counts match, and (c) asserts the null-account guard returns an empty map (no query fired).

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
TransformA batch or streaming data-shaping operation (join/union/enrich).
Streaming transformReal-time transform triggered as events arrive.
Formula fieldLightweight computed value on a DMO.
Calculated insightSQL-derived, persisted KPI object over DMOs; feeds segments/activations.
MeasureA numeric aggregate (SUM, AVG, COUNT).
DimensionA grouping attribute for the insight.
DATEDIFF / DATEADDSQL date functions used in insight time-windows.
GranularityThe level at which an insight is aggregated (per person, per brand).
Unified profile attributeAn insight output column surfaced on the unified profile for filtering/publishing.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can choose batch vs streaming transforms for a scenario.
  • I can write insight SQL with GROUP BY, SUM/AVG/COUNT, DATEDIFF, and date windows.
  • I can list the measures/dimensions for a given KPI and state its granularity.
  • I can explain the sequencing insight → segment → activation.
  • I can extend CalculatedInsightService with a new KPI and a passing test.

Self-Check

  1. Q: Which tool updates a churn counter as online events stream in? — A: A streaming transform (batch transforms only refresh on schedule).
  2. Q: A segment can filter Churn_Score >= 0.7 — where does Churn_Score come from? — A: A previous calculated insight, whose output columns were added as unified-profile attributes.
  3. Q: Why must Total_Spend GROUP BY IndividualId? — A: Granularity must match the question — per-customer spend requires per-individual grouping, not per-order rows.
